conventions.recording: Legacy LeRobot (ManipulatorRobot.teleop_step, `main_*` names): the goal a[t] is WRITTEN to the follower first and the follower state x[t] is READ afterwards (a few ms later), so x[t] may already contain a few ms of response to a[t] (act-then-observe).
conventions.replay: Replay (identical for both conventions): q_sim[0]=x[0] (zero velocity); for t=0..T-2 apply ctrl=a[t-d] (d = fitted integer command delay, stock d=0) for the whole frame, step `substeps` physics steps (timestep set so substeps*timestep = 1/fps exactly), record q_sim[t+1]; sim and real are compared at the same index t=1..T-1. The real sub-frame send-to-read offset (legacy: a[t] sent a few ms BEFORE x[t] is read; current: a[t] sent a few ms AFTER) is not modelled; it is absorbed by the fitted dynamics/delay, and it shifts lags between the two conventions by a fraction of a frame in opposite directions.
conventions.lag: lag = argmin_L Var(a[t] - y[t+L]) over a fixed window t in [0, T-10), parabolic sub-frame refinement; y = real or sim state. Includes the 1-frame sampling offset: in the replay and in observe-then-act (current LeRobot) recordings an instantaneous actuator measures 1.0 frame; in act-then-observe (legacy) recordings it would measure ~0, and a realistic servo measures its delay minus the few-ms write-to-read gap. Lags are therefore directly comparable between sim and real within one dataset, and only approximately (fraction of a frame) across codebases. Also reported in ms, since datasets differ in fps. Joints with command std < 1 deg in an episode are skipped.
conventions.angles: physical degrees (encoder ticks * 360/4096), arm joints only
conventions.change: relative change of an error metric, new/reference - 1; NEGATIVE = better

split.method: future = last round(n*test_frac) episodes by index; interleaved = round(n*test_frac) episodes of the rest drawn by numpy default_rng(seed).permutation, plus every remaining episode beyond the fit cap; fit = the remaining episodes (<= max_train_episodes)
